QUESTION:
Which other drugs interact with Omeprazole?

RESPONSE:
Short answer: the excerpt you've given me only covers the "Uses" and "Directions" sections, so it does not list any drug interactions. I can't cite interaction information from this label text.

For context, the full OTC omeprazole (delayed-release tablet) label normally carries interaction-related warnings such as:

• "Do not use if you are taking a prescription antiretroviral (HIV) medication" — omeprazole can reduce absorption of some HIV drugs (e.g., atazanavir, rilpivirine, nelfinavir).
• "Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are taking" — warfarin (blood thinner), clopidogrel, cilostazol, diazepam, digoxin, tacrolimus, methotrexate, phenytoin, or drugs whose absorption depends on stomach acid (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, iron salts), as well as rifampin or St. John's wort, which can lower omeprazole levels.

Because these specifics are not in the excerpt provided, please check the complete package insert/Drug Facts panel for your product, or ask your pharmacist or prescriber to review your full medication list — especially if you take a blood thinner, an HIV medication, or an anti-seizure or transplant medication.
